quickAnswerHtml: Krua Suwimol is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, in Nakhon Ratchasima, in-town area (Mittraphap Road). Budget around THB 101-250, mostly walk-in with queuing at the door

blocks.html:
Ask anyone from Korat where to go for a late-night congee dinner and the name "Krua Suwimol" comes up fast. This is an open-air, all-night Thai-Chinese congee restaurant on Mittraphap Road, in the Sam Yaek Pak Thong Chai area, that locals have been eating at for so long it's become part of Korat's nightlife. The familiar picture is rows of steel tables, smoke drifting up from the wok every so often, and the sound of spatulas hitting the pan nonstop from the moment the restaurant opens at four in the afternoon until nearly midnight. Then in 2023, this roadside congee restaurant earned a Bib Gourmand from the MICHELIN Guide, and has held onto it through 2026 — which says a lot, since this award goes to restaurants with genuinely good food at prices ordinary people can afford, not fancy places you need to dress up for.

What MICHELIN praises about Krua Suwimol directly is its simple cooking technique paired with very fresh ingredients and bold, intense flavour — which is exactly the heart of Thai-Chinese all-night congee cooking. The dish MICHELIN itself recommends is the fish-sauce fried chicken drumstick, with skin crackling and fragrant with that slightly charred fish-sauce aroma, which goes perfectly with hot congee without needing much thought, plus the stir-fried seafood with holy basil, cooked over such high heat you can taste the wok itself, spicy exactly as the name promises. Beyond those, nearly every table also orders the curry-powder stir-fried crab meat, generous with real crab meat, the crispy fresh water mimosa salad with a punchy, tangy kick, and dozens of other Thai-Chinese congee side dishes to choose from, covering both seafood and made-to-order options. What makes this restaurant fun is that you can order several dishes to share around the table and still end up with a bill that's only a few hundred baht per person. The 4.5/5 score on Tripadvisor confirms it's not just locals who love it — travelers passing through are just as impressed.

The setting adds another layer of charm. Mittraphap Road is the main artery of Isan — almost anyone driving from Bangkok up to Isan has to pass through Korat — and this culture of roadside all-night congee eating is how people in Korat have wound down their day for decades. Families bringing their kids after tutoring classes, groups of friends meeting up after work, and long-haul drivers stopping to refuel before continuing their journey all end up here. MICHELIN picking a restaurant like this for a Bib Gourmand is an acknowledgment that Korat's street food is good enough to be mentioned in the same breath as Bangkok's famous restaurants. If you're passing through Korat in the evening or staying overnight in the city, this restaurant is the answer for a dinner that's easy to eat, genuinely delicious, and gives you the real flavour of Korat without any dressing-up needed.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead at Krua Suwimol?
faq.a: No booking needed — it's walk-in. But if you're coming as a large group or want to check ahead, MICHELIN notes the restaurant takes its own bookings directly — call 044-353-576. Early evening 18:00-20:00 gets busy as usual, so arrive before 18:00 for an easier table

faq.q: About how much per person, and can I pay by card?
faq.a: Around 101-250 THB per person, very light for a Bib Gourmand restaurant. But the restaurant is cash only, so bring enough cash

faq.q: What should I order at Krua Suwimol?
faq.a: The dishes MICHELIN itself recommends are the fish-sauce fried chicken drumstick and the stir-fried seafood with holy basil. Dishes nearly every table orders are the curry-powder stir-fried crab meat, fresh water mimosa salad, and Thai-Chinese style congee side dishes. Ordering several to share around the table is the best way to eat here

faq.q: Where is the restaurant and what are the hours?
faq.a: It's on Mittraphap Road, in the Sam Yaek Pak Thong Chai area, in the city of Nakhon Ratchasima. Open daily 16:00-23:00, with the restaurant's own parking, making it good for both an in-town dinner and a rest stop while driving up or down Isan
